key_findings: Program-wide attendance improved from 78.71% in September to 81.99% in October (+3.28 pp), then held nearly flat at 82.09% in November (+0.10 pp).
The September-to-October gain was meaningful, but the near-flat October-to-November movement means the overall trend is non-monotonic, not a steady upward progression.
The program fell below its 80% attendance goal in September but exceeded it by October and held above it in November.
limitations: The monthly rates are student-level attendance records aggregated across three schools; school-level variation may differ from the program-wide figure.
Two months of post-baseline data is insufficient to establish a reliable trend; the near-flat Oct-to-Nov change could reflect seasonal factors, schedule changes, or sampling noise.
No causal inference is possible from attendance trend data alone.
